title: record form + modal form: an object field visibleWhen naming current_user.hasCapability faults (AppContent / RecordFormPage evaluators omit systemPermissions), while page predicates answer (objectui#13006 follow-up)
body:
Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (seat post objectstack-ai/objectui#9771, session `session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`) from objectui#13006's dev report and its contract review (PR #13081). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Measured (code read at PR #13081's head `2c0b003d70`)

objectui#13006 makes `current_user.hasCapability('NAME')` answer on page predicates. The `ExpressionProvider` scope binds the viewer's `systemPermissions` through objectui#4421's symbol carrier, and `@object-ui/core`'s `evalFieldPredicate` hands it to the engine.

Two surfaces build their object-field evaluator by hand and do not pass the list:
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx`;
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordFormPage.tsx`.

Both call `createExpressionEvaluator({ user, features, permissions: expressionPermissions })`. So an object field's `visibleWhen` naming `hasCapability` faults on the record form and the modal form, while page nodes, nav and actions answer. The fault is loud (reported), never a silent `false`. It is exactly the per-surface hand-off the objectui#4421 comment in `ExpressionProvider` warns about.

## Target

- Each site reads `useExpressionSystemPermissions()` beside `useExpressionPermissions()` and passes it through.
- Pin: a field `visibleWhen: "current_user.hasCapability('X')"` shows for a holder and hides for a non-holder, on the record form and on the modal form.
- Control: not loaded still faults loudly.

## Dedupe

Searched objectui for "hasCapability createExpressionEvaluator RecordFormPage systemPermissions": 0 open hits.
